Subject: Outstanding remittance across entities — VAT and payment routing

Hi Oliver,

Following up on invoice #202611 (attached). Our AP team flagged that the payment hit our US entity account, but for the services you procured the EU entity should be the remit target to satisfy VAT reverse-charge requirements. Because of the mismatch AP routed this to a manual review and the payment is still outstanding.

Could you confirm:
- Whether Atlas intends to remit to Redwood Inference Ltd (UK/EU entity) or to Redwood Inc (US).
- If EU remit: please send a copy of your EU VAT registration or other evidence required by your AP team so we can close the gap.

We can provide a short mutual action plan (MAP) if you need one for your procurement/finance team — I have a draft payment_schedule.xlsx attached that splits the amount by entity and shows the VAT treatment line-by-line.

Next steps I propose: you confirm remit entity and (if applicable) attach VAT evidence; if we don't see a commitment by EOD Friday, I will escalate internally to our Credit team for next steps.

Attachments: Invoice_202611-Atlas.pdf, payment_schedule.xlsx

Thanks,
Mateo Alvarez

Subject: Re: Outstanding remittance across entities — VAT and payment routing

Hi Mateo,

Thanks for the note and the clear breakdown. Apologies — our AP queued this because the PO we received referenced Redwood Inc (US) and our system won't process cross-entity payments without an EU VAT number on file. We've asked AP to hold until we get the VAT evidence.

We're happy to remit to Redwood Inference Ltd if that is the correct entity. Sophie (copied) is our finance lead in Europe and will confirm VAT docs. Can you also confirm whether we need a signed MAP to make the payment flow?

I believe we can clear this once Sophie shares the VAT reg number; will follow up today.

Best,
Oliver
Finance Lead — Procurement, Atlas Biotech

Date: Tue, 03 Nov 2026 14:30:00 -0700
Subject: Fwd: Outstanding remittance across entities — VAT and payment routing (internal)

Team — forwarding Atlas thread. Quick summary: payment in flight but blocked because PO/entity mismatch; they can remit to EU entity once VAT reg is provided.

Proposed handling:
- Marissa: open formal dunning cadence but hold on placing credit hold until we present a constructive offer (MAP).
- Kimberly: confirm what VAT evidence is sufficient for our AR team (EU VAT number, certificate, or a supplier declaration).
- Laura: schedule a 15-min call with Atlas finance (Sophie) if we don't receive the VAT evidence within 24 hours; I can lead it.
- Markus: flagging as a potential exec-level touchpoint if we don't get a commitment by COB Friday — this customer is an active seat expansion opportunity (Deal DL-7812).

Attachments: payment_schedule.xlsx (draft MAP).

I suggest offering a one-time net-15 extension and a small late fee waiver if they sign the MAP and commit to payment date. If no commitment by Friday we escalate to formal collections and consider suspending non-critical integrations.

— Mateo
From: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwoodinference.com>
To: Mateo Alvarez <mateo.alvarez@redwoodinference.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Wed, 04 Nov 2026 10:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Fwd: Outstanding remittance across entities — VAT and payment routing (internal)

Thanks Mateo — agreed with a collaborative first step. Notes from Credit perspective:
- Evidence: EU VAT registration number from Atlas OR a formal supplier VAT certificate should be sufficient to treat this under reverse-charge. Ask Sophie to include the registration country and VAT ID in the reply.
- Collections cadence: open a soft dunning sequence (email + one phone attempt) today; escalate to an official credit hold only after missed commitment date (we should document attempts).
- Legal: if the invoice remains unpaid beyond two weeks after agreed payment date we will initiate contract remedies; loop Legal only if necessary.

Markus — if we don't have confirmation by Friday morning, please be prepared to join a 10-minute exec touchpoint to approve a short freeze on provisioning for non-essential features.

I'll prepare a one-page credit memo summarizing the proposed MAP and the financial risk to share with execs.

Kimberly Park
Head of Credit & Collections, Redwood Inference

Subject: Escalation: Confirm payment date and VAT evidence for Invoice #202611 — action required by 2026-11-10

Hi Oliver / Sophie,

Following our earlier exchanges, we still need the EU VAT registration (or equivalent VAT certificate) to process the invoice under reverse-charge and for Atlas to remit to Redwood Inference Ltd. To avoid further service disruption and internal escalation, please confirm both items by close of business on Tuesday, 2026-11-10:

1) The EU VAT registration number / certificate attached in your reply.
2) A firm payment date (we request payment to settle no later than 2026-11-10).
3) If helpful, sign the attached MAP (signed-MAP.docx) via DocuSign to formalize the payment schedule and waive the late fee as agreed. DocuSign: https://www.docusign.com/en/documents/DS-2026-7812

If we do not receive confirmation by 2026-11-10, per Kimberly's guidance we will move to a formal collections path which may include a credit hold and temporary suspension of non-critical features. We prefer to avoid that and are happy to coordinate a short payment plan if necessary.

Attachments: Invoice_202611-Atlas.pdf, signed-MAP.docx

Thanks for your help — please let me know if you want to jump on a 15-minute call tomorrow.

Regards,
